content.text:
I've opened PR #83 against `dev` for the motion and microinteraction work, and I haven't merged it. The issue is #82. `yarn check`, `yarn typecheck`, `yarn test` (447 pass) and `yarn build` all pass, and the browser showed no console errors or horizontal page overflow at 360, 768, 1280 and 1920px.

**Audit:** the app already had color transitions on buttons and segmented controls, a field focus ring, one chevron rotation and the page spinner. It had no shared timing, no pressed states, a static homepage, silent result changes, a chart you couldn't explore, and an advanced section that snapped open.

**Motion system (`MOTION.md`, tokens in `index.css`):**
- 150, 200, 250 and 400ms durations, two easing curves, and `rise`, `fade`, `wipe` and `flash` animations.
- Only transform, opacity, clip-path and background-color animate, and there is no `transition-all`.
- No animation library was added.

**What now moves:**
- **Homepage:**
  - The hero content enters in a staggered sequence.
  - Sections reveal once as you scroll to them, and stay visible if scripts or animation aren't available.
  - The three clickable tool cards lift on hover and on keyboard focus.
  - The CTA arrows nudge on hover.
- **Controls:** buttons, segmented controls and nav links have pressed and hover feedback, and footer links have hover feedback.
- **Calculator:**
  - The monthly total and cash to close briefly highlight when a new result settles. They never highlight for a stale estimate, on the first value, or on every keystroke.
  - Error messages fade in.
  - The advanced section animates open.
  - Saved scenarios fade in, and schedule rows highlight on hover.
- **Balance chart:** it wipes in once, and a new "Explore the balance by year" slider works by keyboard, touch and pointer. It reads out the exact ledger balance, and the caption and amortization table still carry the data.
- **Left static on purpose:** informational cards have no hover effects.

**Safety:**
- Under reduced motion, nothing is hidden and entrances, reveals and highlights are removed.
- I confirmed this with Chrome's forced reduced-motion flag: no hidden elements, against 8 normally.
- Printing turns all animation off.
- Gzip JS grows by about 0.65kB on the homepage and 0.7kB on the calculator.

**Not verified:**
- I didn't make a GIF, because exporting it downloads a file and I'd need your OK first. The only evidence image is a screenshot of the chart slider at `docs/motion/chart-year-explorer.png`.
- I couldn't test touch emulation or slow-CPU throttling with the tools available.
- I didn't do a full keyboard tab-through or a contrast audit of the changed screens.
- The hero headline now fades in over 400ms, and I didn't measure its effect on LCP.
- The dev server I started earlier may still be running on port 5175.

content.text: The toggles are plain `<button>`s, and Tailwind 4 sets `cursor: default` on buttons. One global rule fixes every interactive control, including the compare Save button.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/styles/index.css'
s=open(p).read()
a='/* `<details>` markers'
b='''/*
 * Tailwind 4 resets buttons to the default cursor. Every enabled control gets
 * the pointer, so toggles, Save, Print and checkbox labels all read as clickable.
 */
:where(
	button:not(:disabled),
	summary,
	select,
	input[type="range"],
	label:has(> input[type="checkbox"]),
	label:has(> input[type="radio"])
) {
	cursor: pointer;
}

'''
assert a in s

content.text:
Every enabled control now shows the pointer cursor: Percent and Dollar amount, the other toggles and Save on the calculator, and Save on the compare page.

In the browser the calculator's 14 enabled buttons all report `pointer`, and the six collapsible summaries do too. Compare's only button, Save, also reports `pointer`.

The cause was Tailwind 4 resetting every `<button>` to the default arrow cursor. I added one global rule in `src/styles/index.css` that gives enabled buttons, summaries, selects, range sliders and checkboxes the pointer. I also gave the PMI checkbox label its own pointer.

I didn't confirm the PMI checkbox or its label, because it only appears when the loan is above 80% of the price and the default scenario has none. Disabled buttons keep the normal arrow.

`yarn check`, `yarn typecheck` and `yarn test` (447 pass) all pass. I added this as commit `bdf0258` on the same branch, so PR #83 now includes it. It still isn't merged.

content.text:
All buttons and toggles now highlight their background and lift 2px on hover, then shrink slightly on press. I confirmed the hover lift in the browser (a 2px rise on the Dollar amount toggle, with its background tinting). I couldn't hold the mouse button down there, so the press shrink isn't confirmed. `yarn check`, `yarn typecheck` and `yarn test` (447 pass) all pass, and the change is pushed to PR #83.

- **Buttons:** Save, Print report, Calculate and the other CTAs, whether button or link. On hover they get a 2px lift and a darker or lighter fill. On press they drop back and shrink to 0.97. Disabled buttons don't move.
- **Toggles:** Percent / Dollar amount, the `$` / `% of price` toggles on tax, insurance and HOA, Monthly / Yearly, and the Fixed-rate / ARM and loan-term choices. Unselected ones get a white highlight on hover, the selected one gets a soft tint, and they lift and shrink the same way. This covers the Save button on the compare page too.
- **Transition fix:** Tailwind 4 moves things with `translate` and `scale`, not `transform`, so the transition lists only covered `transform`. The movement would have snapped. I fixed that, including for the homepage tool cards from the earlier motion work, so they now ease as well.
- **Reduced motion:** the lift and shrink are off, and the background highlight stays.

I changed only the shared style files, so nothing else was touched. The toggle group is tight, so a 2px lift sits close to its edge. If it looks cramped, 1px for toggles is a one-line change.

<pasted_content id="fe23">
Act as a Senior Product Designer and Principal React Engineer.

Project: Mortgage Calculator
Repository: wajidalii/mortgage-calculator
Base branch: dev

Redesign the Compare Loans page to provide an intuitive, interactive, side-by-side mortgage comparison experience.

## Main requirement

On desktop, display Loan A and Loan B side by side, with independent editable inputs and corresponding results.

Users should be able to visually compare both options without constantly scrolling between separate forms or result cards.

## UI/UX requirements

1. Build a responsive two-column comparison workspace.
2. Each column should contain its own loan inputs, principal and interest, estimated monthly ownership costs, upfront expenses, and long-term interest results, where supported by the existing engine.
3. Align corresponding fields and metrics between the two columns.
4. Clearly distinguish Loan A and Loan B through consistent headings and subtle visual styling.
5. Update results immediately when valid inputs change.
6. Allow users to edit either loan without unexpectedly changing the other.
7. Add a Swap Loans action.
8. Add a Duplicate Loan A to Loan B action to simplify comparisons.
9. Display a concise comparison summary showing differences in monthly payment, lifetime interest, and other comparable metrics.
10. Use subtle emphasis for the lower numerical value, but do not automatically label one loan as universally better.
11. Include a shared assumption indicator where values differ or comparison assumptions are not equivalent.
12. Preserve the distinction between fixed-rate and ARM estimates, including hypothetical future-rate warnings.
13. Avoid duplicating or rewriting the financial calculation engine.

## Desktop layout

At 1024px and above:
- Loan A on the left.
- Loan B on the right.
- Matching input and result sections aligned.
- A comparison summary visible without excessive scrolling.
- Clear visual separation between loans.
- Optional sticky summary headers when useful.

## Mobile layout

At smaller widths:
- Do not force two cramped columns.
- Provide accessible Loan A / Loan B switching or stacked cards.
- Keep a compact differences summary available.
- Preserve both loans' values when switching views.
- Ensure all inputs remain usable on 360px screens.

## Visual design

Use your own professional design judgment.

Follow the application's existing design system and motion language.

Add purposeful hover, focus, selection, and transition effects, without distracting from financial information.

## Quality requirements

- Preserve all existing comparison calculations and business rules.
- Avoid unnecessary dependencies.
- Use React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and existing components.
- Keep comparison state understandable and independently testable.
- Support keyboard and screen-reader navigation.
- Test different loan terms, rates, principal amounts, and loan types.
- Ensure no horizontal page overflow.
- Run yarn check, yarn typecheck, yarn test, and yarn build.
- Perform browser tests at 360px, 768px, 1280px, and 1920px.
- Capture desktop and mobile screenshots.

## GitHub workflow

Review existing comparison-related issues and PRs before making changes.

Create a new UX issue only if this work is not already tracked.

Create a feature branch from the latest dev, implement the improvements, and open a PR targeting dev.

Do not merge without my approval.

Start by auditing the existing Compare Loans page, then implement the side-by-side experience.
</pasted_content id="fe23">

- [ ] Keyboard order follows one loan at a time; status messages for swap and copy

- [ ] Version 1 saved comparisons open correctly

content.text:
The Compare Loans page is rebuilt as a side-by-side workspace. PR #85 is open against `dev` and not merged; the issue is #84.

`yarn check`, `yarn typecheck`, `yarn test` (460 pass) and `yarn build` all pass. In the browser there is no horizontal overflow at 360, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1920px.

**What it does**
- **Desktop (1024px and up):** Loan A and Loan B sit side by side. Their sections line up row for row, even when one loan is an ARM and has extra fields. Each column header stays pinned and shows that loan's monthly total.
- **Below 1024px:** one loan shows at a time, with a sticky Loan A / Loan B switch that displays both monthly totals. Switching keeps both loans' values.
- **Independent loans:** price, down payment, loan type, term, rate and ARM index path belong to each loan. Editing B never changes A.
- **Results:**
  - Each loan shows principal and interest, tax, insurance, PMI and total monthly cost.
  - Each loan shows loan amount, down payment, cash to close and lifetime interest.
  - These come from the calculator's own functions, so no calculation was rewritten.
- **Actions:**
  - **Swap loans** and **Copy Loan A to Loan B** are both there.
  - A screen reader announces each action.
- **Summary:**
  - "Differences at a glance" states each gap in plain words, for example "Loan B is $956.16 lower".
  - Lower values get a small "Lower" tag, and nothing is called "better".
  - Notes tagged "Differs" or "Shared" flag different prices, down payments or terms, a fixed-versus-ARM mismatch, and the shared assumptions.
- **ARM:** the "Hypothetical rate" label and the assumed index path stay visible.
- **Tab order:** it goes through all of Loan A, then all of Loan B.

**Decisions to review**
- Price and down payment are no longer shared, per your brief. Comparing two loans on the same home now means entering the price twice, and Copy Loan A to Loan B is the shortcut. A "same home" toggle would be a small follow-up if you want it.
- To make the independent inputs work I changed the saved-scenario format, and old saved comparisons are upgraded when they load. A test covers that.
- Property-tax state, insurance and PMI use the calculator's defaults and can't be edited on this page. The page says so.
- Saved scenarios now sit below the comparison so the summary and both loans appear higher.
- The column wrapper is a labelled `div` with a documented lint exception, because Chrome can't line up rows through a `<fieldset>`.

**Not verified**
- Touch emulation, CPU throttling, other browsers, and a real screen reader.
- The first commit's engine change was committed before the UI caught up, so it may not typecheck on its own. The branch head passes.

Screenshots at 360, 768, 1280 and 1920px, plus a Loan B ARM view, are in `docs/compare/`. The dev server I started earlier may still be running on port 5175.
